4. Autumn has camouflage OR blends, but not both (original).
5. Autumn has camouflage OR unique wings, but not both (original).
6. Every butterfly that attracts attention has unique wings (added rule).  So attracting attention ⇒ unique wings (but NOT the converse).
7. We possess no premise that gives Autumn unique wings in every case, nor any chain that forces her to have them.  Case analysis:
   - Case A: Assume Autumn has vibrant wings.
     – Then by (2) she does not blend.
     – From (4) she must then have camouflage (and not blend).
     – From (5) with camouflage true, unique wings must be false (exclusive or).  Hence she lacks unique wings.
     – From (6) she therefore cannot attract attention.
   - Case B: Assume Autumn lacks vibrant wings.
     – From (1) she then has a delicate pattern.
     – From (3) with vibrant wings false, she must have mottled color.
     – Mottled color ⇒ she blends (original rule).
     – Blending ⇒ by (4) she lacks camouflage.
     – From (5) with camouflage false, she must have unique wings (exclusive or).
     – Having unique wings satisfies the necessary condition for attracting attention, but no premise supplies the sufficient direction (unique wings ⇒ attracts attention is NOT stated).  So in this case we are still uncertain whether she attracts attention.

Because in Case A we can definitively construct a consistent scenario in which Autumn does NOT attract attention, the premises do not entail that she must attract attention.  Therefore the conclusion is not entailed; the correct choice is False.
